subject: Acceptance evidence ledger: control/data demarc + runbook asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Carter <nate.carter@acmecloud.com>, ops@racknode.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: Acceptance evidence ledger: control/data demarc + runbook asks

Nate / RackNode team —

Thanks again for walking through the on‑prem topology yesterday. Before we sign off the deployment acceptance for the initial pilot cluster, we need a tight evidence ledger documenting the control-plane / data-plane demarc, egress proofing, and a short cutover runbook. Specifically we need: 

- A single-page reference diagram that highlights the demarcation points (TLS/mTLS boundaries, control-plane endpoints, KV cache proxy locations, and egress NAT). PDF preferred.
- A short ops cutover runbook (Excel or Sheets) with steps, expected durations, rollback criteria and alerting hooks.
- A checklist proving egress isolation (what IPs are allowed, which services require outbound access, and where telemetry is exfiltrated).
- Evidence of key management: how KMS/HSM is reached from the control plane (network path and ACLs).

Can you produce those artifacts by EOD tomorrow (2026-08-19) so our Security and Ops teams can validate? We will collate into the acceptance evidence bundle and attach to the HubSpot deal.

Action items for Redwood: Marissa — assemble the acceptance template. Kim — prepare the runbook skeleton with our standard probes/alerts. Neha — we'll need a short note on compliance/regulatory constraints to include.

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

[attachments: none yet]

From: Nate Carter <nate.carter@acmecloud.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@racknode.io, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T13:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Acceptance evidence ledger: control/data demarc + runbook asks

Jonas / team —

Appreciate the clear list. Attached are three artifacts to start: control-data-demarc_v1.pdf (diagram), ops-cutover-runbook.xlsx (runbook draft), and a short egress checklist (egress-proof-checklist.md). High level notes below: 

- Diagram: shows control plane API endpoints terminating in the management VLAN (10.3.0.0/24) with mTLS to runtime nodes in tenant VLANs. KV cache proxy is colocated with the runtime nodes behind the data‑only load balancer.
- Runbook: a 12‑step cutover sequence with time estimates, smoke tests, and explicit rollback to previous staging cluster. We included a step that toggles a traffic‑mirror for 10 minutes to validate KV cache correctness.
- Egress checklist: lists outbound endpoints (KMS, Docker registry, metrics backhaul) and suggests a minimal NAT gateway approach plus an outbound filter on the router.

Two clarifying points we need from Redwood before finalizing: 
1) Which KMS provider will be authoritative for the pilot (your KMS endpoint or customer‑managed HSM)? That affects ACLs shown on page 2 of the PDF.
2) Confirm whether telemetry (prometheus push gateway) is allowed to egress over the same NAT or must use a dedicated proxy.

I've placed the artifacts on the RackNode SFTP and shared a Drive link in the egress checklist header. If this is adequate we can finalize for your Security review.

Regards,
Nate Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer — RackNode Solutions

[attachments: control-data-demarc_v1.pdf (stub), ops-cutover-runbook.xlsx (stub), egress-proof-checklist.md (stub)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Carter <nate.carter@acmecloud.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Acceptance evidence ledger: control/data demarc + runbook asks

Nate — thanks, the artifacts look like a great starting point. Quick notes from Redwood ops/security: 

- We prefer customer‑managed HSM for this pilot — can we get the HSM IP ranges and any mutual auth steps documented? If not, we will default to Redwood KMS with a scoped service account for the pilot.
- For telemetry, Security prefers a dedicated proxy endpoint (to give per‑tenant filtering and egress logging). Can RackNode suggest a lightweight proxy we can run in the management VLAN?
- Runbook: please add an explicit step for validating KV cache warmup and a tokenized smoke test that asserts <95ms tail latency for the first 100 requests from a mirror agent.

Marissa will pull these artifacts into the acceptance template and we will run a quick checklist pass. Kim — can you add the probe details to the runbook (I flagged the cell). Neha — please draft a one‑page compliance note we can attach.

Thanks — Marissa
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

[attachments: none]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Nate Carter <nate.carter@acmecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Tina Patel <tina@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Acceptance evidence ledger: control/data demarc + runbook asks

Thanks — a couple of quick clarifications before Security does their pass: 

- HSM: if RackNode can provide IP ranges and the TCP ports used for the HSM management channel, we can map ACLs. If customer HSM is not available, Redwood KMS is acceptable but we'll need an uptime SLA note.
- Proxy: we like the idea of a dedicated telemetry proxy. Can RackNode share a short container image name and a small example ingress rule? If the proxy supports TLS termination to the metrics endpoint that would be ideal.

Timing: once we have the HSM ranges and a one‑line proxy recommendation, we can complete the evidence bundle and schedule a Security readout on Friday (2026‑08‑21) at 16:00 PT. Is that workable for RackNode?

Jonas
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-19T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Acceptance evidence ledger: control/data demarc + runbook asks

Jonas / team —

We can commit to the Friday readout (2026‑08‑21, 16:00 PT). Quick delivery notes attached: 

- HSM/IP ranges: attached in control-data-demarc_v1.pdf (page 2). Ports: 443 and 15001 for management tunnel.
- Telemetry proxy: recommend "racknode/metrics-proxy:1.2.0" (small container, TLS passthrough to remote backhaul). Example ingress rule included in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1abcdExampleDiagram
- SLA: For pilot, RackNode will provide a 99.5% management-channel SLA and will agree to a ticketed escalation path. We will put a short note into the DocuSign amendment (link above).

We'll update the Excel runbook with the HSM IP ranges and add the probe details you requested. Let us know if you want us to host a 30‑minute run through of the runbook prior to the Security readout.

Thanks — Tina
Head of Integrations — RackNode Solutions
